supersedes: version 2 (bar.json) for the split redesign only. The rule is Kane's switch-on bar unchanged; what is new is the held-out set it is scored on and that the baseline is the BEST of the non-Jev readings, not only the word match. The old 62 (labels.json) were used to tune the redesign and are scored for information only.
rule: Jev reads data questions for Pro only when ALL hold on fresh-labels.json, run once: (1) Jev beats the best non-Jev baseline: more items Jev gets right and that baseline gets wrong than the other way round, with an exact two-sided McNemar test on those discordant items at p < mcnemarAlpha; (2) Jev makes no more harmful mistakes than that baseline, a harmful mistake being a reading settled with confidence that is wrong and would run, so it returns a plausible number (wrongRan). The best baseline is the one with the most right items on this set, ties broken by fewer harmful mistakes. A reading Jev is not sure of must say so and run nothing; it counts as not right and is never harmful. A decline item is right when nothing is settled, and harmful when a reading runs.

baselines.words: the word match (JevQueryWordArm.Read): closest measures and columns by name, exact value matches, top N from the words
baselines.shortlist: the word match with every split replaced by the engine's own split shortlist, top pick first (JevQueryWordArm.ReadShortlist): the redesign's shortlist with no Jev
